title: Does the winter South China Sea Warm Current exist, and what drives it
query: In winter the northern South China Sea shelf is often reported to carry a northeastward current against the northeasterly monsoon (the South China Sea Warm Current), but studies disagree about whether it persists and what drives it. Using the supplied CMOMS daily velocity, temperature and salinity for 2011-2020, determine whether, where and when such a countercurrent exists in winter, how persistent it is, and which proposed driving mechanisms the data support.
